sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kṛtodakās te suhṛdāṃ sarveṣāṃ pāṇḍunandanāḥ viduro dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca sarvāś ca bharatastriyaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the sons of Pāṇḍu, together with Vidura and Dhṛtarāṣṭra and all the women of the Bharatas, had made the water-offerings for all their kinsmen,

sanskrit: tatra te sumahātmāno nyavasan kurunandanāḥ śaucaṃ nivartayiṣyanto māsam ekaṃ bahiḥ purāt
english: those great-souled delights of the Kurus dwelt there for one full month outside the city, to complete the rites of purification.

sanskrit: kṛtodakaṃ tu rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram abhijagmur mahātmānaḥ siddhā brahmarṣisattamāḥ
english: And to the righteous-souled king Yudhiṣṭhira, who had performed the water-rite, there came great souls, perfected ones, the most excellent of brahmin-sages.

sanskrit: dvaipāyano nāradaś ca devalaś ca mahān ṛṣiḥ devasthānaś ca kaṇvaś ca teṣāṃ śiṣyāś ca sattamāḥ
english: Dvaipāyana and Nārada and Devala that mighty seer, Devasthāna and Kaṇva, and the most excellent of their disciples;

sanskrit: anye ca vedavidvāṃsaḥ kṛtaprajñā dvijātayaḥ gṛhasthāḥ snātakāḥ sarve dadṛśuḥ kurusattamam
english: and other twice-born ones, learned in the Vedas, of perfected wisdom, householders and graduates all alike, came to behold the best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: abhigamya mahātmānaḥ pūjitāś ca yathāvidhi āsaneṣu mahārheṣu viviśus te maharṣayaḥ
english: Having approached and been honored according to custom, those great-souled mighty seers took their places upon seats of great worth.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tataḥ pūjāṃ tatkālasadṛśīṃ tadā paryupāsan yathānyāyaṃ parivārya yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Then, having received the homage suited to that hour, they sat in attendance, encircling Yudhiṣṭhira as was fitting.

sanskrit: puṇye bhāgīrathītīre śokavyākulacetasam āśvāsayanto rājānaṃ viprāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: On the holy bank of the Bhāgīrathī the brahmins, in their hundreds of thousands, sought to console the king whose mind was distraught with grief.

sanskrit: nāradas tv abravīt kāle dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram vicārya munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ tatkālasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ
english: And Nārada, in due time, having taken counsel with the sages, addressed the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira in words befitting that hour:

sanskrit: bhavato bāhuvīryeṇa prasādān mādhavasya ca jiteyam avaniḥ kṛtsnā dharmeṇa ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: "By the might of your arm, by the grace of Mādhava, and by righteousness, this whole earth has been won, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā muktāḥ stha saṃgrāmād asmāl lokabhayaṃkarāt kṣatradharmarataś cāpi kaccin modasi pāṇḍava
english: By good fortune you have come safe through this battle that struck terror into the world. Devoted as you are to the duty of the warrior, do you now rejoice, O son of Pāṇḍu?

sanskrit: kaccic ca nihatāmitraḥ prīṇāsi suhṛdo nṛpa kaccic chriyam imāṃ prāpya na tvāṃ śokaḥ prabādhate
english: Having slain your foes, do you gladden your friends, O king? And having attained this sovereign fortune, does grief no longer torment you?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vijiteyaṃ mahī kṛtsnā kṛṣṇabāhubalāśrayāt brāhmaṇānāṃ prasādena bhīmārjunabalena ca
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This whole earth has been conquered, resting upon the strength of Kṛṣṇa's arm, by the grace of the brahmins, and by the might of Bhīma and Arjuna.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu me mahad duḥkhaṃ vartate hṛdi nityadā kṛtvā jñātikṣayam imaṃ mahāntaṃ lobhakāritam
english: Yet this great sorrow abides in my heart unceasingly: that I have wrought this vast destruction of my own kinsmen, all of it born of greed.

sanskrit: saubhadraṃ draupadeyāṃś ca ghātayitvā priyān sutān jayo 'yam ajayākāro bhagavan pratibhāti me
english: Having caused the deaths of Subhadrā's son and the sons of Draupadī, my dear children, this victory, O blessed one, appears to me to wear the face of defeat.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vakṣyati vārṣṇeyī vadhūr me madhusūdanam dvārakāvāsinī kṛṣṇam itaḥ pratigataṃ harim
english: What will the Vṛṣṇi-maiden, my daughter-in-law, say to Madhusūdana — to Kṛṣṇa, to Hari, the dweller in Dvārakā — when he returns hence to her?

sanskrit: draupadī hataputreyaṃ kṛpaṇā hatabāndhavā asmatpriyahite yuktā bhūyaḥ pīḍayatīva mām
english: This Draupadī, her sons slain, her kinsmen slain, wretched, ever devoted to our love and welfare, torments me yet the more.

sanskrit: idam anyac ca bhagavan yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi nārada mantrasaṃvaraṇenāsmi kuntyā duḥkhena yojitaḥ
english: And there is this other thing, O blessed Nārada, of which I shall speak to you: by the keeping-secret of a counsel, I have been yoked to sorrow by Kuntī.

sanskrit: yo 'sau nāgāyutabalo loke 'pratiratho raṇe siṃhakhelagatir dhīmān ghṛṇī dānto yatavrataḥ
english: He who had the strength of ten thousand elephants, in this world a warrior without an equal in battle, who moved with the sporting gait of a lion, wise, compassionate, self-controlled, firm in his vows;

sanskrit: āśrayo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ mānī tīkṣṇaparākramaḥ amarṣī nityasaṃrambhī kṣeptāsmākaṃ raṇe raṇe
english: the refuge of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, proud, fierce in valor, impatient of insult, ever ardent for the fray, our reviler in battle after battle;

sanskrit: śīghrāstraś citrayodhī ca kṛtī cādbhutavikramaḥ gūḍhotpannaḥ sutaḥ kuntyā bhrātāsmākaṃ ca sodaraḥ
english: swift with his weapons, a varied fighter, accomplished, of wondrous prowess — he was Kuntī's son, born in secret, and our own brother, of the same womb.

sanskrit: toyakarmaṇi yaṃ kuntī kathayām āsa sūryajam putraṃ sarvaguṇopetam avakīrṇaṃ jale purā
english: He whom Kuntī, at the water-rite, declared to be the son of Sūrya — her own son, endowed with every virtue, cast away of old upon the waters.

sanskrit: yaṃ sūtaputraṃ loko 'yaṃ rādheyaṃ cāpy amanyata sa jyeṣṭhaputraḥ kuntyā vai bhrātāsmākaṃ ca mātṛjaḥ
english: He whom all this world deemed the charioteer's son and called Rādheya — he was Kuntī's eldest son, and our brother, born of the same mother.

sanskrit: ajānatā mayā saṃkhye rājyalubdhena ghātitaḥ tan me dahati gātrāṇi tūlarāśim ivānalaḥ
english: By me, not knowing, greedy for the kingdom, he was brought to his death in battle. That burns my limbs as fire burns a heap of cotton.

sanskrit: na hi taṃ veda pārtho 'pi bhrātaraṃ śvetavāhanaḥ nāhaṃ na bhīmo na yamau sa tv asmān veda suvrataḥ
english: For not even Pārtha of the white steeds knew him for his brother, nor I, nor Bhīma, nor the twins — yet he, true to his vows, knew us.

sanskrit: gatā kila pṛthā tasya sakāśam iti naḥ śrutam asmākaṃ śamakāmā vai tvaṃ ca putro mamety atha
english: We have heard that Pṛthā went to him, desiring peace between us, and said, 'You too are my son.'

sanskrit: pṛthāyā na kṛtaḥ kāmas tena cāpi mahātmanā atipaścād idaṃ mātary avocad iti naḥ śrutam
english: But Pṛthā's wish was not granted by that great-souled one; rather, at the very last, he said this to his mother, so we have heard:

sanskrit: na hi śakṣyāmy ahaṃ tyaktuṃ nṛpaṃ duryodhanaṃ raṇe anāryaṃ ca nṛśaṃsaṃ ca kṛtaghnaṃ ca hi me bhavet
english: 'I cannot forsake King Duryodhana in battle; that would be ignoble in me, cruel, and an act of ingratitude.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhireṇa saṃdhiṃ ca yadi kuryāṃ mate tava bhīto raṇe śvetavāhād iti māṃ maṃsyate janaḥ
english: 'If, by your will, I were to make peace with Yudhiṣṭhira, men would think me afraid of him of the white steeds in battle.'

sanskrit: so 'haṃ nirjitya samare vijayaṃ sahakeśavam saṃdhāsye dharmaputreṇa paścād iti ca so 'bravīt
english: 'When I have conquered in the field Vijaya together with Keśava, then afterward I shall make peace with the son of Dharma' — so he said.

sanskrit: tam avocat kila pṛthā punaḥ pṛthulavakṣasam caturṇām abhayaṃ dehi kāmaṃ yudhyasva phalgunam
english: Then Pṛthā, it is said, spoke again to that broad-chested one: 'Grant safety to four of them; fight Phalguna if you will.'

sanskrit: so 'bravīn mātaraṃ dhīmān vepamānaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ prāptān viṣahyāṃś caturo na haniṣyāmi te sutān
english: And the wise one answered his mother, trembling, with folded hands: 'Even when I have them in my power and can withstand them, I will not slay those four sons of yours.

sanskrit: pañcaiva hi sutā mātar bhaviṣyanti hi te dhruvam sakarṇā vā hate pārthe sārjunā vā hate mayi
english: Five sons, O mother, shall surely remain to you in any case: either with Karṇa if Pārtha falls, or with Arjuna if I fall.'"

sanskrit: taṃ putragṛddhinī bhūyo mātā putram athābravīt bhrātṝṇāṃ svasti kurvīthā yeṣāṃ svasti cikīrṣasi
english: Then his mother, longing for her sons, spoke to her son once more: 'Do good to your brothers, you who wish to do them good.'

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā tu pṛthā visṛjyopayayau gṛhān so 'rjunena hato vīro bhrātā bhrātrā sahodaraḥ
english: Having spoken thus to him, Pṛthā took her leave and went home; and that hero was slain by Arjuna — brother by brother, born of the same womb.

sanskrit: na caiva vivṛto mantraḥ pṛthāyās tasya vā mune atha śūro maheṣvāsaḥ pārthenāsau nipātitaḥ
english: Neither Pṛthā's secret nor his own was ever disclosed, O sage; and so that valiant great archer was struck down by Pārtha.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tv ajñāsiṣaṃ paścāt svasodaryaṃ dvijottama pūrvajaṃ bhrātaraṃ karṇaṃ pṛthāyā vacanāt prabho
english: Only afterward did I learn, O best of the twice-born, from Pṛthā's own words, O lord, that Karṇa was my elder brother, born of the same womb.

sanskrit: tena me dūyate 'tīva hṛdayaṃ bhrātṛghātinaḥ karṇārjunasahāyo 'haṃ jayeyam api vāsavam
english: By this my heart is sorely pained, a slayer of my brother; for with Karṇa and Arjuna for my helpers I could have vanquished even Vāsava himself.

sanskrit: sabhāyāṃ kliśyamānasya dhārtarāṣṭrair durātmabhiḥ sahasotpatitaḥ krodhaḥ karṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā praśāmyati
english: When I was being tormented in the assembly hall by the evil-souled sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the anger that suddenly rose in me would grow calm at the mere sight of Karṇa.

sanskrit: yadā hy asya giro rūkṣāḥ śṛṇomi kaṭukodayāḥ sabhāyāṃ gadato dyūte duryodhanahitaiṣiṇaḥ
english: For even when I heard his harsh words, bitter in their import, spoken in the assembly at the gambling-match, he desiring Duryodhana's good —

sanskrit: tadā naśyati me krodhaḥ pādau tasya nirīkṣya ha kuntyā hi sadṛśau pādau karṇasyeti matir mama
english: even then my anger would vanish when I gazed upon his feet; for Karṇa's feet were like Kuntī's — such was my thought.

sanskrit: sādṛśyahetum anvicchan pṛthāyās tava caiva ha kāraṇaṃ nādhigacchāmi kathaṃ cid api cintayan
english: Seeking the cause of that likeness between him and Pṛthā, I could find no reason for it, however much I pondered.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu tasya saṃgrāme pṛthivī cakram agrasat kathaṃ ca śapto bhrātā me tat tvaṃ vaktum ihārhasi
english: How was it that in battle the earth swallowed his chariot-wheel? And how was my brother cursed? This you ought to tell me here.

sanskrit: śrotum icchāmi bhagavaṃs tvattaḥ sarvaṃ yathātatham bhavān hi sarvavid vidvāṃl loke veda kṛtākṛtam
english: I wish to hear from you, O blessed one, the whole of it exactly as it was; for you, all-knowing and learned, know in this world what has been done and what has not.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa evam uktas tu munir nārado vadatāṃ varaḥ kathayām āsa tat sarvaṃ yathā śaptaḥ sa sūtajaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the sage Nārada, best of speakers, related the whole of it — how that son of the charioteer had been cursed.

sanskrit: evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi bhārata na karṇārjunayoḥ kiṃ cid aviṣahyaṃ bhaved raṇe
english: "It is even so, O mighty-armed Bhārata, as you say: for Karṇa and Arjuna there was nothing in battle that could not be borne or overcome.

sanskrit: guhyam etat tu devānāṃ kathayiṣyāmi te nṛpa tan nibodha mahārāja yathā vṛttam idaṃ purā
english: But this is a secret of the gods, which I shall tell you, O king. Hear it then, O great king, as it came to pass of old.

sanskrit: kṣatraṃ svargaṃ kathaṃ gacchec chastrapūtam iti prabho saṃgharṣajananas tasmāt kanyāgarbho vinirmitaḥ
english: 'How may the warrior caste go to heaven, purified by the sword?' — with this purpose, O lord, one who would breed strife was fashioned, conceived in the womb of a maiden.

sanskrit: sa bālas tejasā yuktaḥ sūtaputratvam āgataḥ cakārāṅgirasāṃ śreṣṭhe dhanurvedaṃ gurau tava
english: That child, endowed with splendor, came to the state of a charioteer's son, and learned the science of archery under your teacher, the best of the Āṅgirasas.

sanskrit: sa balaṃ bhīmasenasya phalgunasya ca lāghavam buddhiṃ ca tava rājendra yamayor vinayaṃ tathā
english: The strength of Bhīmasena, and the deftness of Phalguna, and your wisdom, O lord of kings, and the discipline of the twins —

sanskrit: sakhyaṃ ca vāsudevena bālye gāṇḍivadhanvanaḥ prajānām anurāgaṃ ca cintayāno vyadahyata
english: and the friendship of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva with Vāsudeva from boyhood, and the affection of the people — brooding on all these, he was consumed inwardly.

sanskrit: sa sakhyam agamad bālye rājñā duryodhanena vai yuṣmābhir nityasaṃdviṣṭo daivāc cāpi svabhāvataḥ
english: In his boyhood he formed a friendship with King Duryodhana, ever at enmity with you — both by destiny and by his own nature.

sanskrit: vidyādhikam athālakṣya dhanurvede dhanaṃjayam droṇaṃ rahasy upāgamya karṇo vacanam abravīt
english: Then, perceiving that Dhanaṃjaya surpassed him in learning in the science of arms, Karṇa came in secret to Droṇa and spoke these words:

sanskrit: brahmāstraṃ vettum icchāmi sarahasyanivartanam arjunena samo yuddhe bhaveyam iti me matiḥ
english: 'I wish to learn the brahma-weapon, together with its secret and its withdrawal; it is my desire to become Arjuna's equal in battle.

sanskrit: samaḥ putreṣu ca snehaḥ śiṣyeṣu ca tava dhruvam tvatprasādān na māṃ brūyur akṛtāstraṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ
english: Surely your affection for your sons and your disciples is equal; by your grace, let not the discerning call me unaccomplished in arms.'

sanskrit: droṇas tathoktaḥ karṇena sāpekṣaḥ phalgunaṃ prati daurātmyaṃ cāpi karṇasya viditvā tam uvāca ha
english: Droṇa, thus addressed by Karṇa, mindful of Phalguna and knowing too the evil bent of Karṇa, said to him:

sanskrit: brahmāstraṃ brāhmaṇo vidyād yathāvac caritavrataḥ kṣatriyo vā tapasvī yo nānyo vidyāt kathaṃ cana
english: 'A brahmin who has duly fulfilled his vows may know the brahma-weapon, or a warrior who is an ascetic; no other may know it on any account.'

sanskrit: ity ukto 'ṅgirasāṃ śreṣṭham āmantrya pratipūjya ca jagāma sahasā rāmaṃ mahendraṃ parvataṃ prati
english: Thus addressed, he took leave of the best of the Āṅgirasas and, paying him reverence, went straightway to Rāma upon Mount Mahendra.

sanskrit: sa tu rāmam upāgamya śirasābhipraṇamya ca brāhmaṇo bhārgavo 'smīti gauraveṇābhyagacchata
english: Approaching Rāma and bowing with his head, he came to him with reverence, saying, 'I am a brahmin of the Bhārgava line.'

sanskrit: rāmas taṃ pratijagrāha pṛṣṭvā gotrādi sarvaśaḥ uṣyatāṃ svāgataṃ ceti prītimāṃś cābhavad bhṛśam
english: Rāma received him, having asked him fully of his lineage and the rest, and said, 'Be welcome; dwell here.' And he was exceedingly pleased with him.

sanskrit: tatra karṇasya vasato mahendre parvatottame gandharvai rākṣasair yakṣair devaiś cāsīt samāgamaḥ
english: While Karṇa dwelt there upon Mahendra, the best of mountains, there was for him fellowship with gandharvas and rākṣasas, yakṣas and gods.

sanskrit: sa tatreṣv astram akarod bhṛguśreṣṭhād yathāvidhi priyaś cābhavad atyarthaṃ devagandharvarakṣasām
english: There he gained mastery over weapons, in due form, from the best of the Bhṛgus, and became exceedingly dear to the gods, the gandharvas, and the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa kadā cit samudrānte vicarann āśramāntike ekaḥ khaḍgadhanuṣpāṇiḥ paricakrāma sūtajaḥ
english: Once, wandering by the seashore near the hermitage, alone, with sword and bow in hand, the son of the charioteer roamed about.

sanskrit: so 'gnihotraprasaktasya kasya cid brahmavādinaḥ jaghānājñānataḥ pārtha homadhenuṃ yadṛcchayā
english: And there, O Pārtha, unknowingly and by mere chance, he killed the sacrificial cow of a certain brahmin given to the fire-oblation, a knower of the Veda.

sanskrit: tad ajñānakṛtaṃ matvā brāhmaṇāya nyavedayat karṇaḥ prasādayaṃś cainam idam ity abravīd vacaḥ
english: Reckoning the deed to have been done in ignorance, Karṇa confessed it to the brahmin, and seeking to appease him, spoke these words:

sanskrit: abuddhipūrvaṃ bhagavan dhenur eṣā hatā tava mayā tatra prasādaṃ me kuruṣveti punaḥ punaḥ
english: 'Without intent, O blessed one, this cow of yours has been slain by me; in this, grant me your grace' — so he said again and again.

sanskrit: taṃ sa vipro 'bravīt kruddho vācā nirbhartsayann iva durācāra vadhārhas tvaṃ phalaṃ prāpnuhi durmate
english: But that brahmin, enraged, said to him, reviling him as it were with his speech: 'You wretch of evil conduct, you deserve death; reap your fruit, you of evil mind!

sanskrit: yena vispardhase nityaṃ yadarthaṃ ghaṭase 'niśam yudhyatas tena te pāpa bhūmiś cakraṃ grasiṣyati
english: With that very one whom you ceaselessly seek to rival, for whose sake you strive day and night — when you fight with him, O sinful one, the earth shall swallow your chariot-wheel.

sanskrit: tataś cakre mahīgraste mūrdhānaṃ te vicetasaḥ pātayiṣyati vikramya śatrur gaccha narādhama
english: And when your wheel is swallowed by the earth, your foe shall surge forward and strike off the head of you, bewildered. Go, basest of men!

sanskrit: yatheyaṃ gaur hatā mūḍha pramattena tvayā mama pramattasyaivam evānyaḥ śiras te pātayiṣyati
english: As this cow of mine was slain by you in your heedlessness, O fool, even so shall another strike off your head when you are heedless.'

sanskrit: tataḥ prasādayām āsa punas taṃ dvijasattamam gobhir dhanaiś ca ratnaiś ca sa cainaṃ punar abravīt
english: Then he sought again to appease that best of the twice-born with cows and wealth and jewels; but the brahmin spoke to him once more:

sanskrit: nedaṃ madvyāhṛtaṃ kuryāt sarvaloko 'pi vai mṛṣā gaccha vā tiṣṭha vā yad vā kāryaṃ te tat samācara
english: 'Not even the whole world could make this utterance of mine false. Go or stay, or whatever you must do, do it.'

sanskrit: ity ukto brāhmaṇenātha karṇo dainyād adhomukhaḥ rāmam abhyāgamad bhītas tad eva manasā smaran
english: Thus told by the brahmin, Karṇa, his face cast down in misery, came to Rāma in fear, brooding upon that very curse in his heart.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca karṇasya bāhuvīryeṇa praśrayeṇa damena ca tutoṣa bhṛguśārdūlo guruśuśrūṣayā tathā
english: Nārada said: By the might of Karṇa's arm, by his modesty and self-restraint, and by his service to his teacher, the tiger of the Bhṛgus was well pleased.

sanskrit: tasmai sa vidhivat kṛtsnaṃ brahmāstraṃ sanivartanam provācākhilam avyagraṃ tapasvī sutapasvine
english: To him that ascetic, calmly and in full, taught the entire brahma-weapon, complete with its withdrawal, in due form — to that ardent striver.

sanskrit: viditāstras tataḥ karṇo ramamāṇo ''śrame bhṛgoḥ cakāra vai dhanurvede yatnam adbhutavikramaḥ
english: Then Karṇa, accomplished in arms and taking his ease in the hermitage of the Bhṛgu, applied himself to the science of archery, he of wondrous prowess.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid rāmas tu carann āśramam antikāt karṇena sahito dhīmān upavāsena karśitaḥ
english: Then one day the wise Rāma, walking near the hermitage in Karṇa's company, worn thin by fasting,

sanskrit: suṣvāpa jāmadagnyo vai visrambhotpannasauhṛdaḥ karṇasyotsaṅga ādhāya śiraḥ klāntamanā guruḥ
english: the son of Jamadagni lay down to sleep — that teacher, weary of mind, his affection grown from trust — resting his head upon Karṇa's lap.

sanskrit: atha kṛmiḥ śleṣmamayo māṃsaśoṇitabhojanaḥ dāruṇo dāruṇasparśaḥ karṇasyābhyāśam āgamat
english: Then a worm, born of phlegm, a feeder upon flesh and blood, dreadful and dreadful to the touch, came near to Karṇa.

sanskrit: sa tasyorum athāsādya bibheda rudhirāśanaḥ na cainam aśakat kṣeptuṃ hantuṃ vāpi guror bhayāt
english: Reaching his thigh, that drinker of blood pierced it through; yet Karṇa could neither cast it off nor slay it, for fear of waking his teacher.
